name: Camera response shaping
summary: Camera deadzones, acceleration, recentering, framing, and optional movement effects translate physical input into perception and aim.
player_action: The player aims, turns, changes speed, enters a constrained space, or tracks a target.
system_response: The camera applies declared response curves and framing rules while protecting visibility, comfort, and aiming intent.

conflicts_with: automatic motion that overrides aiming during threats

failure_modes: Acceleration prevents consistent flick or tracking distances.
Automatic recentering fights deliberate camera placement.
Head bob, shake, or field-of-view shifts induce discomfort or obscure aim.
accessibility: Expose sensitivity, acceleration, deadzone, inversion, recentering, shake, bob, blur, and field-of-view controls when relevant.
Keep gameplay outcomes stable when comfort effects are disabled.
Test mouse, multiple controllers, and keyboard-only camera alternatives.

smallest_playable_test.setup: A target-tracking lane, 90- and 180-degree turns, a narrow corridor, an occluding wall, and a sprint section with live response-curve controls.
smallest_playable_test.retain_if: Players can predict camera displacement, track targets, and preserve orientation without discomfort under supported devices.
smallest_playable_test.revise_if: One device class or spatial condition produces systematic overshoot, delay, or discomfort.
smallest_playable_test.reject_if: Automatic camera behavior repeatedly overrides player intent or makes required aiming unreliable.

evidence.claim: Insomniac's Resistance 3 aiming presentation identifies camera acceleration and deadzoning as basic camera movement systems that interact with shooter gameplay and mission structure.
evidence.notes: GDC session overview by Insomniac Games.

evidence.claim: Destiny's first-person presentation treats camera motion as part of the persistent motion set supporting responsive, physical embodiment.

notes: Aim assistance is related but is not included as an assumed requirement in this record.
